images.title: Adding steps against doubling folds
images.purpose: Compares a ladder of 20 cm steps that needs 1922000000 steps to reach the Moon with paper folds that need only 46 doublings.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A before and after comparison: a ladder on the left and a paper stack on the right, both reaching one dashed line at the top.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal reddish purple (#CC79A7) dashed line across the top labelled Moon: 384400 km. Left half: a tall thin teal (#0072B2) ladder reaching the dashed line, labelled linear above its foot, with + 20 cm each step beside it and 1922000000 steps under it. Right half: an amber (#E69F00) column of folded paper layers reaching the dashed line, labelled exponential above its foot, with × 2 each fold beside it and 46 folds under it. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Adding the same amount is slow; multiplying reaches the Moon in just 46 steps.

image_decisions.why: Side by side, the ladder and the folds show linear against exponential growth.
